paper.title_en: Entanglement-link geometry in asymmetric W-class states and emergence of super-link fragility
paper.abstract_en: The asymmetric three-qubit W-class state $|\overline{W_3^L}\rangle $ has an isosceles entanglement-network geometry: its two vertex-base (VB) links are stronger than both its base-base (BB) link and the bipartite links of the symmetric $|W\rangle $ state, suggesting that such a concentrated super-link may benefit quantum-network tasks. We show analytically that this intuition is incomplete. Comparing $|W\rangle $ and $|\overline{W_3^L}\rangle $, which differ in both geometry and excitation sector, we find that the noiseless hierarchy $\mathcal {C}_{VB}>\mathcal {C}_W>\mathcal {C}_{BB}$ is preserved under phase damping without entanglement sudden death (ESD). Under amplitude damping it is reordered: $|W\rangle $ becomes the most robust, and $\mathcal {C}_{BB}$ vanishes at $\gamma =1/2$. We term this the Super-Link Fragility Effect. For a continuous isosceles family, the effect occurs throughout the super-link domain $1/\sqrt{6}<a<1/\sqrt{3}$, where the vertex-base advantage is lost at $\gamma _{\textrm{cross}}(a)=[1-1/(3a\sqrt{1-2a^2})]^2$; the original state $a=1/2$ maximizes both the initial super-link concurrence and this threshold. Under depolarization, $\mathcal {C}_W$ and $\mathcal {C}_{VB}$ share the ESD threshold $p=3/8$, while $\mathcal {C}_{BB}$ vanishes earlier at $p=3/10$. The generalized amplitude damping channel interpolates to the pure-excitation limit, where $\mathcal {C}_{VB}$ and $\mathcal {C}_{BB}$ keep their initial ordering without ESD, whereas $\mathcal {C}_W$ undergoes ESD at $p=4/9$. Entanglement robustness in W-class resources is thus governed jointly by network geometry, excitation sector, and noise symmetry, not by initial concurrence alone.
